post.description: Request a swap quote based on input parameters such as the assets, amount, slippage tolerance, and recipient/refund information. Requests are rate limited per API key.

dry.description:
Flag indicating whether this is a dry run request.

If `true`, the response will NOT contain the following fields:

- `depositAddress`

- `timeWhenInactive`

- `deadline`

swapType.description:
How to interpret `amount` (and refunds) when performing the swap:

- `EXACT_INPUT` — requests the output amount for an exact input.

  - If deposit is less than `amountIn`, the deposit is refunded by deadline.

  - If deposit is above than `amountIn`, the swap is processed and the excess is refunded to refundTo address after swap is complete.

- `EXACT_OUTPUT` — requests the input amount for an exact output.

  - The quote response includes `minAmountIn` and `maxAmountIn`.

  - If the input is above `maxAmountIn`, the swap is processed and the excess is refunded to `refundTo` after the swap is complete.

  - If the input is below `minAmountIn`, the deposit is refunded by deadline.

- `FLEX_INPUT` — a flexible input amount that allows for partial deposits and variable amounts.

  - `slippage` applies both to `amountOut` and `amountIn` and defines an acceptable range (`minAmountIn` and `minAmountOut`).

  - Any amount higher than `minAmountIn` is accepted and converted to the output asset as long as `minAmountOut` is met.

  - `amountIn` can be less, as long as the 'slippage + 1%' constraint is met. If the total received by the deadline is below the lower bound, the deposit is refunded.

  - If deposits exceed the upper bound, the swap is still processed.

depositType.description:
Type of deposit address:

- `ORIGIN_CHAIN` - deposit address on the origin chain.

- `INTENTS` - the account ID within NEAR Intents to which you should transfer assets.

- `CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS` - the account ID within Confidential Intents to which assets are to be transferred. Fund the swap from a Confidential Intents account by submitting a signed transfer intent to the quote `depositAddress`. Direct token transfers are not supported.

depositMode.description:
What deposit address mode you will get in the response.

Most chains support only `SIMPLE`, and some (for example `stellar`) only `MEMO`:

- `SIMPLE` - usual deposit with only a deposit address.

- `MEMO` - some chains require the `memo` together with `depositAddress` for the swap to work.

quoteWaitingTimeMs.description:
Time in milliseconds the user is willing to wait for a quote from the relay.

Use `0` to request the fastest available quote.

confidentiality.description:
Confidentiality mode for this quote (defaults to `public`):

- `public` - the swap is settled on public Intents rails.

- `basic` / `advanced` - the swap is settled on Confidential Intents rails.

amount.description: Amount to swap as the base amount, in the smallest unit of the currency. It is interpreted as input or output based on `swapType`.

slippageTolerance.description: Slippage tolerance for the swap in basis points (1/100th of a percent), e.g. 100 for 1%.

refundType.description:
Type of refund address:

- `ORIGIN_CHAIN` - assets are refunded to the `refundTo` address on the origin chain.

- `INTENTS` - assets are refunded to the `refundTo` Intents account.

- `CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS` - assets are refunded to the `refundTo` Confidential Intents account. On Confidential Intents, 1Click settles refunds via signed transfer intent rather than direct token transfer.

recipient.description: Recipient address. The format must match `recipientType`.

recipientType.description:
Type of recipient address:

- `DESTINATION_CHAIN` - assets are transferred to the chain of `destinationAsset`.

- `INTENTS` - assets are transferred to an account inside Intents.

- `CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS` - assets are transferred to the `recipient` account inside Confidential Intents. On Confidential Intents, 1Click settles swap output via signed transfer intent rather than direct token transfer.

- `REFUNDED` - the deposit was refunded.

- `FAILED` - the swap failed.

post.description:
Returns a chain-specific deposit address that funnels deposits into the recipient's account. The same address is returned for repeat calls with the same API key + recipient + sender + depositChain + destinationChain/destinationAsset + confidential, so users can safely save it externally. A different API key (or `destinationAsset`/`destinationChain`/`confidential`) yields a different deposit address and a separate underlying Intents account.

> **Access.** Creating new addresses is limited to organisations approved by Aurora; any other API key receives a 403.

> **EVM chains share one address.** Across different EVM chains you only need to generate the deposit address **once** using any EVM chain as `depositChain`. The returned address works automatically for deposits on every other supported EVM chain — no need to call this endpoint again per EVM chain.

> **Fees.** The account is minted with a baseline of app fees computed like `/api/quote` from the key's fee configuration (confidential variants when `confidential` is true). Because the deposited asset is not known yet, only fee rules that do not constrain the origin asset apply, matched against the destination. The fees actually applied to each swap come from `/api/persistent-deposit-fees`, which 1Click calls per swap with the real origin asset.

recipient.description: Target address on the destination chain. Funds deposited to the returned address will ultimately route to this address.

sender.description: Identifier of the user the deposit address is generated for (e.g. their ID in the system). A unique deposit address is generated and persisted per (API key, sender, recipient, destinationAsset, confidential, depositChain), so incoming deposits can be attributed to a specific user. A single underlying Intents account is shared per (API key, sender, recipient, destinationAsset, confidential) across all deposit chains; only the deposit address is chain-specific.

depositChain.description: Chain the user deposits FROM (the chain of the returned deposit address). Short code matching the widget config Chains enum, e.g. "arb" for Arbitrum. The special value "evm" is accepted as a shortcut for any EVM chain — all EVM chains share one deposit address — and resolves to Base ("base"). For "stellar", the response includes a `memo` that deposits must carry. "qtc" (native QTC) is disabled by default: only available to API keys whose organisation Aurora has allowed the `qtc` asset group.

destinationChain.description: Chain the user receives funds ON. Used to resolve `destinationAsset` when it is provided as a symbol. Short code matching the widget config Chains enum, e.g. "base" for Base.

destinationAsset.description: Asset the user wants to receive on `destinationChain`. Accepts either a token symbol (e.g. "USDC") or an asset ID (e.g. "nep141:base-0x...omft.near"). When a symbol is used and more than one token shares that symbol on `destinationChain`, the request is rejected with 400 and the caller must switch to the asset ID.

confidential.description: Whether the underlying account used for swaps settles on the Confidential Intents rail. When `true`, the account is minted with basic confidentiality mode (deposits still arrive at ordinary chain addresses). Part of the address identity: `true` and `false` produce different, independently persisted deposit addresses and separate accounts for otherwise identical parameters. Defaults to `false`.

schema.description:
To specify the asset the user receives, you can either:
- Pass a token **symbol** in `destinationAsset` (e.g. "USDC") together with `destinationChain` (e.g. "base"). The API resolves the symbol to an asset ID on that chain.
- Or pass an **asset ID** directly in `destinationAsset` (e.g. "nep141:base-0x...omft.near"). `destinationChain` is still required to locate it.

When a symbol matches more than one token on the same `destinationChain`, the request fails with `400` and an error listing the matching asset IDs ("Multiple tokens with symbol ... Use one of the asset IDs instead: ..."). In that case, retry with the specific asset ID you want.

get.description: Failed-swap monitor (two-phase). VERIFY-FIRST: each run first drains up to MONITOR_VERIFY_BATCH globally-queued TO_BE_CHECKED accounts (re-read balance, enrich via Explorer → 1Click → persistent, Slack-alert) — but only those queued at least MONITOR_VERIFY_DELAY_SECONDS ago, so funds still moving through a healthy swap are not reported as stuck. If nothing has ripened it SCANS the next MONITOR_SCAN_BATCH accounts of one referral (stalest-first, resumable via sweep_cursor) — one cheap balance read each — queueing every non-zero account for verification. Pass `referral` to force a scan of a specific one. Triggered by cron or an admin.
